question: Find a unit vector in the direction of $(\hat{i}+\hat{j})\times(\hat{i}+\hat{k})$. Verify that the obtained vector is perpendicular to both given vectors.
explanation:
Step 1: Evaluation of the vector product
Let $\vec{a}=\hat{i}+\hat{j}$ and $\vec{b}=\hat{i}+\hat{k}$. Then
\(\vec{a}\times\vec{b}=\begin{vmatrix}\hat{i}&\hat{j}&\hat{k}\\1&1&0\\1&0&1\end{vmatrix}=\hat{i}-\hat{j}-\hat{k}\)
Step 2: Magnitude of the cross product
\(|\vec{a}\times\vec{b}|=\sqrt{1^2+(-1)^2+(-1)^2}=\sqrt{3}\)
Step 3: Required unit vector
\(\hat{n}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}(\hat{i}-\hat{j}-\hat{k})\)
Step 4: Perpendicularity verification
\(\hat{n}\cdot\vec{a}=\frac{1-1}{\sqrt{3}}=0,\qquad\hat{n}\cdot\vec{b}=\frac{1-1}{\sqrt{3}}=0\)
Final Answer
The required unit vector is $\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}(\hat{i}-\hat{j}-\hat{k})$.

options.A: $\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}(\hat{i}-\hat{j}-\hat{k})$; its scalar product with both $\hat{i}+\hat{j}$ and $\hat{i}+\hat{k}$ is zero.
options.B: $\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}(\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k})$; it is perpendicular to both given vectors.
options.C: $\frac{1}{3}(\hat{i}-\hat{j}-\hat{k})$; it is a unit vector perpendicular to both.
options.D: $\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}(\hat{i}-\hat{j})$; it is perpendicular to both given vectors.
